technical_and_design_decisions: Use existing Hyperledger Fabric SDK structure as a reference for the Node SDK implementation.
Follow the API design outlined in FAB-687 for the new-channel configuration transaction.
Implement peer upgrade logic with backward compatibility to ensure no data loss during protocol changes.
Refactor ledger tests to remove explicit dependencies on MSP security modules.
Integrate sanity checks for LCCC and chaincode invocations into the core chaincode execution logic.
Structure documentation to clearly differentiate between v0.6 (stable) and v1.0 (under development) features.
assumptions: The existing codebase has a modular architecture that can be extended for new features.
The Node SDK will be implemented as a standalone module with minimal dependencies on other components.
Visual aids and scripts for U5 will be created as separate deliverables, not integrated into the core codebase.
The ledger test refactoring (U4) will not require changes to production ledger code.
The sanity checks (U7) will be implemented as part of the chaincode invocation validation layer.
Documentation updates (U1, U6) will be written in parallel with code development.

activities.activity_description: Create documentation for new visitors (U1) and update v1.0 documentation while directing users to v0.6 for stability (U6).
Implement the API for creating new-channel configuration transactions as described in FAB-687 (U2).
Develop peer upgrade logic to support protocol changes without data loss, including chaincode lifecycle and SCC patches (U3).
Fix ledger code to use the new block structure and remove dependencies on MSP security modules in tests (U4).
Create visual diagrams and scripts to explain Fabric v1.0 architecture and behavior (U5).
Implement validation logic to ensure only LCCC or normal chaincode can be invoked (U7).
Develop a Node.js SDK for interacting with the blockchain (U8).
